exposure: indications for obstetric hysterectomy (abnormal placentation, post-partum haemorrhage, uterine atony, rupture)
cohort: The study included 30 patients who underwent obstetric hysterectomy at a tertiary care centre.
finding: Most morbidity associated with obstetric hysterectomy is attributed to the indications for which it is done rather than the procedure itself, with abnormal placentation becoming the most common indication.
mod_finding: The study suggests focusing on reducing the rate of caesarean sections whenever possible to improve outcomes.
